squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition launches wide-ranging operation against Houthi forces in Yemen, says 136 military targets destroyed
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition says it is conducting a broad operation against Houthi capabilities in Yemen and has destroyed 136 military targets in areas the group controls. The inputs do not report any market reaction.

squawks.headline: Russia lifts diesel export restrictions with immediate effect and offers extra supply to the US and other partners, Novak says
squawks.detail: Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Moscow welcomes US steps to stabilise global energy markets and is ready to supply additional diesel to the US and all partners as early as October. He said exports should rise further in November and December as refineries return from maintenance, and that the domestic market will remain fully supplied.

squawks.headline: S&P affirms UK sovereign rating at AA/A-1+ with a stable outlook
squawks.detail: S&P Global Ratings affirmed the UK's 'AA/A-1+' ratings with a stable outlook and raised its 2026 UK real GDP growth estimate to 1.3%, citing a stronger-than-expected first half. The agency said oil, gas and other input prices linked to the Middle East conflict, such as fertiliser, are affecting inflation and interest rates.

squawks.headline: Trump says Russia will supply diesel to world markets after Putin call; US Treasury issues temporary licence to allow it
squawks.detail: After a call with President Putin, Trump said Russia will supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel immediately, another 500,000 tons in November and 1,000,000 tons after that, followed by 3,000,000 tons within a short period, depending on the condition of its refineries. The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control said it is issuing a temporary general licence, effective immediately, to allow Russian diesel to be supplied to the global market.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kazaks says 2.5% is the top of neutral and the ECB is in a fairly comfortable position on rates
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said 2.5% marks the upper limit of the ECB's neutral range and that the European economy is relatively resilient to shocks.

squawks.headline: US Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins climb to 1.5m b/d, or 72% of production, MMA data show
squawks.detail: MMA data show 1.5m b/d of US Gulf of Mexico oil output is now shut in, which is 72% of production. The previous reading was 1.3m b/d, or 63%.

squawks.headline: Saudi Aramco to supply full contracted oil volumes to European customers in November
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reports that Saudi Aramco will deliver full oil volumes to its European customers for November. No further figures were given.

squawks.headline: US Michigan sentiment drops to 46.3 in preliminary October reading, below 47.6 forecast; 1-year inflation expectations at 4.7%
squawks.detail: The University of Michigan's preliminary October sentiment index came in at 46.3, against a forecast of 47.6 and 48.1 previously, while the expectations index rose to 47.3 against a 45.7 forecast. One-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6% (forecast 4.8%), and five-year expectations rose to 3.5% from 3.4%, matching the forecast.

squawks.headline: University of Michigan preliminary current conditions index falls to 44.7, short of the 50.1 forecast
squawks.detail: The preliminary University of Michigan current conditions reading for the US came in at 44.7. The forecast was 50.1 and the previous reading was 50.9.

squawks.headline: White House sets up committee to investigate allegations of false statements by Fed Governor Lisa Cook
squawks.detail: In a statement, the White House said President Trump has set up a committee of inquiry to look into allegations that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook made false statements.

squawks.headline: Canada sheds 68.3k jobs in September against a forecast 10k gain; unemployment rate rises to 6.5%
squawks.detail: Canadian employment fell by 68.3k in September after a 41.7k fall the previous month, and the jobless rate rose to 6.5% from 6.4%, in line with forecast. The participation rate slipped to 64.8%, while average hourly earnings growth picked up to 2.3% year on year, matching the forecast, from 2.0%.

squawks.headline: Germany to release up to 15m barrels of oil and petroleum products from reserves under the G7 stock release deal
squawks.detail: Germany's economy minister says diesel and heating oil will be released first, followed by crude oil. The minister also says Germany will fully implement the G7 agreement on releasing energy stocks.

squawks.headline: IMF says global government debt could reach 100% of GDP by 2028, a level not seen since World War II
squawks.detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said advanced economies are the largest contributors to the rise. She said it is unrealistic to count on stronger growth to reduce debt burdens.

squawks.headline: Bank of Spain lifts its 2026 inflation forecast to 3.9% and its 2027 forecast to 3.7% from 2.7%
squawks.detail: The Bank of Spain raised its 2026 growth forecast to 2.6% from 2.3% and its 2027 forecast to 2.2% from 1.7%. It expects a budget deficit of 2.6% in 2026 and public debt of 98.5% of GDP at the end of 2026, and named geopolitics, oil prices and rising bond yields as risks to the outlook.

squawks.headline: Yemeni government forces reportedly take control of Bab al-Mandeb, with Saudi envoy saying the strait is cleared of Houthis
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia's ambassador to Yemen is reported as saying Houthi forces have been cleared from the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Separate reports say Yemeni government forces have taken control of Bab al-Mandeb and Mayun. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: China and EU reach understanding on hybrid vehicle trade and agree to manage trade disputes, China's commerce ministry says
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry said the hybrid vehicle deal follows intensive negotiations and complies with WTO rules, and that talks will continue on price undertakings in the EU's anti-subsidy probe into Chinese electric vehicles. It also said China will keep looking at lowering tariffs on some goods under WTO rules, will keep speeding up rare earth and permanent magnet export licences to the EU, and that the two sides will hold their next regular meeting in March 2027.

squawks.headline: UK retail footfall falls 2.9% in September, a steeper drop than August's 1.7% decline, BRC data show
squawks.detail: The British Retail Consortium's figures show total UK retail footfall fell 2.9% in September, compared with a 1.7% fall the previous month, City AM reports.

squawks.headline: Japanese government bond yields fall, with 10-year down 5.5bp to 3.025%
squawks.detail: In Asian trading the 10-year JGB yield fell 5.5bp to 3.025%. The 5-year yield fell 4bp to 2.345% and the 30-year fell 6bp to 4.060%.

squawks.headline: German Bund futures rise 0.45% and French OAT futures 0.78% in Asian trading
squawks.detail: Euro area government bond futures gain in early Friday trading. Reuters reports that France's debt market has stabilised after its recent sell-off and that US yields have fallen.

squawks.headline: Heavy explosions reported in the southern Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian media blaming tankers hitting mines
squawks.detail: Iran's Fars news agency cites military sources as reporting heavy explosions in the southern Strait of Hormuz, which it says were caused by tankers striking mines. The inputs report no market reaction yet.

squawks.headline: European Commission rejects Italian and Greek requests for more fiscal rules flexibility to cover energy-driven inflation
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the European Commission on Thursday turned down requests from Italy and Greece for extra fiscal leeway for euro zone governments over energy-driven inflation and support measures. The Commission said the rules could not be changed all the time.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle 4.07% higher at $104.28 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures closed the session up $4.08 at $104.28 a barrel, a gain of 4.07% on the day.

squawks.headline: WTI crude futures settle 3.64% higher at $91.49 a barrel
squawks.detail: NYMEX November WTI crude futures settled up $3.21, or 3.64%, at $91.49 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.8829 a gallon.

squawks.headline: Oil prices surge as Houthis strike Riyadh for a second day and Iran steps up attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that Yemen's Houthis carried out missile strikes on the Saudi capital for a second day, while Iran increased the pace of its attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices were reported as surging; no figure was given.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says further policy firming will be needed to return inflation to target, sees rates rising in next 6 to 9 months
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said inflation is elevated, driven by persistent demand pressures and supply shocks, and that limiting second-round effects is key. He said his contacts are mostly worried about inflation rather than the job market, and that he goes into every meeting with an open mind.

squawks.headline: US Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins rise to 1.3m b/d, or 63% of production, MMA data show
squawks.detail: Figures attributed to MMA put shut-in US Gulf oil output at 1.3m b/d, or 63% of the region's production. An earlier figure put shut-ins at 511,619 b/d, about 25% of output.

squawks.headline: US $22bn 30-year bond auction tails by 0.1bp at 5.618%; bid-to-cover falls to 2.54
squawks.detail: The US Treasury's $22bn 30-year auction had a high yield of 5.618%, against 5.617% in when-issued trading and 5.308% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover was 2.54, down from 2.61, with indirect bidders taking 72.32%, directs 20.89% and primary dealers 6.79%.

squawks.headline: US sanctions 17 vessels for carrying Iranian crude, oil products and petrochemicals
squawks.detail: The US Treasury Department announced new Iran-related sanctions covering dozens of people, entities and vessels. A Treasury official said Iran has stopped loading and offloading crude vessels because of the US blockade and sanctions, and estimated that 20 million barrels of Iranian crude remain on vessels outside the blockade.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says the ECB has tools to counter unwarranted market dynamics and is paying attention to markets
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde made the remarks to Euro Finance Chief. She also said she sees no sign that price rises are broadening.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections and reports productive talks with Tehran
squawks.detail: The US President said the US would not strike Iran ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November and described discussions with Iran as productive. The posts reported no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Forecasts put the UK energy price cap 16% higher for Q1 2027, Resolution Foundation says
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the latest forecasts show the Q1 2027 energy price cap 16% higher, approaching the peak levels capped in 2022 and 2023.

squawks.headline: US publishes its diesel executive order in the Federal Register
squawks.detail: The US administration has published the diesel executive order in the Federal Register. No further details of what the order contains were given.

squawks.headline: UK and EU agree to link their carbon emissions trading systems, Politico reports
squawks.detail: Politico reports that the UK and the EU have reached an agreement to link their emissions trading systems.

squawks.headline: NatWest Markets quits European and US primary dealer roles but stays on as a gilt-edged market maker
squawks.detail: IFR reports that NatWest Markets is giving up its primary dealerships for six European sovereigns, the EU and the US following a review of its markets business. It will keep its UK role as a Gilt-Edged Market Maker.

squawks.headline: EU reminded its primary dealers of their market-making obligations on Monday as bond volatility peaked, IFR reports
squawks.detail: IFR reports that the European Union contacted its primary dealers on Monday after extreme volatility led banks to cut their quoting to the minimum required, to limit potential losses.

squawks.headline: Riksbank Governor Thedéen says there are grounds for an interest rate increase
squawks.detail: Riksbank Governor Erik Thedéen said there are grounds for raising interest rates, according to a newswire headline. No further detail was given.

squawks.headline: WTO raises 2026 global goods trade forecast to 3.9% from 1.9% but cuts its services trade outlook
squawks.detail: The World Trade Organization now forecasts global goods trade growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027, up from a 1.9% estimate for 2026 in March, and global economic growth of 2.6% in 2026. It lowered its 2026 services trade forecast, citing disruption to transport and travel from the Middle East conflict.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says fiscal policy must be credible and fiscal commitments matter more than ever after negative shocks
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor said fiscal policy must be credible and aimed at stability, and that fiscal commitments are needed most when negative shocks hit. He also said the Bank cannot be at all relaxed about large and concentrated market positions or the risk of wider disruption.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says markets show an elevated risk premium and the Bank must test for a significant shock to inflation expectations
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey also said markets remain resilient and that he is fully committed to bringing inflation back to target.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey sees subdued evidence so far of energy costs feeding wider inflation, but says risks grow the longer prices stay high
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said there was currently little evidence of higher energy costs passing through into broader inflation, but that risks remain. He added that inflation risks increase the longer high energy prices persist.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says market moves are some way from normal but finds no illiquidity or stressed conditions
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said market movements are well away from normal. He added that the Bank is not seeing illiquidity or stressed conditions, as the global bond sell-off continues to hit gilts.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey calls for more resilient core markets and says greater absorption of government debt has brought more fragility
squawks.detail: In a speech, the Bank of England Governor said central clearing, minimum haircuts and better risk management deserve consideration, and that monetary policy must stay firmly committed to bringing inflation back to target. He also said repeated shocks and higher government debt make it harder for governments to cushion a downturn, and warned of a shock if expectations for AI are sharply revised.

squawks.headline: French Finance Minister Lescure says the bond market is not dysfunctional
squawks.detail: France's finance minister said bond markets are not dysfunctioning, as French and other high-debt European government bond yields climb in a global sell-off.

squawks.headline: ECB accounts say a 2.50% deposit rate is still within staff estimates of neutral and warn against guidance on the rate path
squawks.detail: The ECB's account of its latest policy meeting says officials thought it particularly important not to give guidance on future rates, wanted the policy response to stay proportionate and stressed continued vigilance. The account also says risks did not all point the same way and that monetary policy transmission has been smooth.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield rises above last week's high as other high-debt European bond yields climb with it
squawks.detail: An economist reports that France's 10-year government bond yield has moved past the previous high it set a week ago, with yields across other high-debt European countries also rising. No new yield level was given.

squawks.headline: BoE survey shows UK lenders cut mortgage availability for the first time in three years
squawks.detail: A Bank of England survey released on Thursday shows that in the three months to the end of August, UK lenders reduced the supply of mortgages and other secured lending to households. It is the first such reduction in three years.

squawks.headline: UK announces sanctions on Russian oil companies and tankers
squawks.detail: The UK has imposed new sanctions on Russian oil companies and tankers. The report gave no further details.

squawks.headline: ECB's Stournaras sees no significant second-round inflation effects and says inflation expectations remain anchored near 2%
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Stournaras said he does not see important second-round effects. He also said inflation expectations are well anchored at around 2%.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says she is worried by the UK pay outlook, with employers on track for pay rises of about 3.5% next year
squawks.detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said on Thursday that pay rises of around 3.5% next year would be larger than is helpful for bringing inflation back to the 2% target, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: UK 20-year gilt yield reaches 6% for the first time since March 1998, up 7bp on the day
squawks.detail: A market news account reported that the UK 20-year gilt yield hit 6%, its first time at that level since March 1998, up 7bp on the day. The move came as the global bond sell-off continued.

squawks.headline: Brent crude extends its rise to 5% on the day and trades above $105 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent's gain widened to 5%, taking it above $105 a barrel. The blotter earlier reported it topping $101 after more attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

squawks.headline: UK 10-year gilt yield rises to 5.515%, its highest since July 2007, up more than 6bp on the day
squawks.detail: The 10-year gilt yield reached 5.515%, its highest level since July 2007, after rising more than 6bp on the day.

squawks.headline: European Commission says Italy can use the national escape clause from EU fiscal rules for energy
squawks.detail: European Commission spokespeople said Italy may invoke the national escape clause in the EU fiscal rules to cover energy-related spending.

squawks.headline: Germany raises its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 1.3% from 0.5% and its 2027 forecast to 1.1% from 0.9%
squawks.detail: The German Economy Ministry more than doubled its 2026 growth forecast, citing a rally in manufacturing. It forecasts 2028 GDP growth of 0.6%.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane expects food prices to face upward pressure next year and says central banks should be believed on inflation returning to target
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said the ECB expects upward pressure on food prices over the next year. He also said central banks should be believed when they say inflation will return to target.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene sees a material risk that some second-round inflation effects may develop
squawks.detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene warned of a material risk of second-round effects emerging, according to a market news feed on 8 October.

squawks.headline: BoE's Pill calls current price pressures concerning and says they must be tackled
squawks.detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said current price pressures are a concern and need to be addressed, according to a market newswire headline.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says more rate rises are needed, though they need not come at back-to-back meetings
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Waller said inflation is too high, pointing to the AI buildout and the continuing energy shock as persistent pressures, and that he expects further rises if data come in as expected. He also said inflation has been above target for nearly 5-1/2 years, putting expectations at risk, and called the September labour market solid and stable even though job creation slowed.

squawks.headline: SNB Vice Chairman Martin attributes the recent rise in Swiss inflation to oil products
squawks.detail: Swiss National Bank Vice Chairman Martin said the recent increase in Swiss inflation is due to oil products. He also said the Swiss franc has weakened recently but has stayed stable in real terms since 2020.

squawks.headline: ECB's Dolenc sees upside inflation risks from oil, gas, food and strong growth; steadier core offers some reassurance
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Dolenc said inflation risks are tilted to the upside because of oil, gas, food and strong growth. He added that more stable core inflation gives some comfort that wider price pressures remain contained.

squawks.headline: ECB's Wunsch says the case for raising the minimum reserve requirement is unclear and unconvincing
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Pierre Wunsch questioned the reasoning behind raising banks' minimum reserve requirement. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says euro area inflation is entirely energy-driven and sees no second-round effects
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said the ECB faces an inflationary shock, euro area inflation is 100% energy and second-round effects are not visible. He also said the geopolitical shock is feeding through into a financial shock.

squawks.headline: ECB's Sleijpen describes the energy shock as fairly persistent
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Olaf Sleijpen said the energy price shock is proving persistent. No further detail or market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: German trade surplus narrows to 19.5bn, above 19bn forecast; exports fall 0.8% m/m against a forecast 0.9% rise
squawks.detail: Germany's seasonally adjusted trade balance came in at 19.5bn, compared with a forecast of 19bn and 21.3bn previously. Exports fell 0.8% m/m, the same as the previous month. Imports rose 0.9%, short of the 2.8% forecast, after a 5.7% fall previously.

squawks.headline: US oil futures rise more than 2% to $90.07 a barrel on storm and shipping supply risks
squawks.detail: US crude futures gained more than 2% to $90.07 a barrel in early trading on worries about the storm and shipping supply. The US National Hurricane Center had earlier said Isaias had strengthened into a hurricane.

squawks.headline: BoJ regional report finds firms passing on higher costs and some raising prices more often
squawks.detail: In its regional economic report, the Bank of Japan said firms in many regions are passing on higher costs from the Middle East conflict, the weak yen and labour, and many are keeping wage offers high. It also said strong global AI-related demand is lifting output.

squawks.headline: KPMG/REC survey shows UK permanent staff placements rising at their fastest pace in four years in September
squawks.detail: The KPMG/REC survey of recruitment firms, published on Thursday, shows more signs of the UK labour market recovering from its long slowdown in September.

squawks.headline: UK RICS house price balance falls to -32% in September, weaker than the -30% expected and down from -28%
squawks.detail: The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors reports that downward pressure on house prices increased in September for the first time in four months. It said the prospect of higher interest rates weighed on the housing market.

squawks.headline: Iran says it and Oman have agreed coordinates for safe transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Iran and Oman, as coastal states, agreed the geographical coordinates of safe transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz and how to present the agreement internationally. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: FT estimates the Iran war has cut UK public finances by nearly £12bn, roughly halving Chancellor Healey's fiscal headroom
squawks.detail: FT estimates find that higher inflation and borrowing costs have probably cut the Chancellor's headroom by about half. The FT says this leaves him relying on tax rises and spending cuts at the Budget to help with living costs.

squawks.headline: US Gulf of Mexico oil output of 511,619 b/d shut in, about 25% of the region's production
squawks.detail: Figures attributed to the MMA show 511,619 barrels a day of US Gulf oil production shut in, equal to 25.08% of output. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Diesel prices jump after the IEA says no fuel will be released beyond the stock release agreed in March
squawks.detail: The FT reports that IEA members say the 100mn barrels promised by the G7 will come out of the 400mn barrel release agreed in March, not from additional stocks. Diesel prices are reported to have jumped in response; no figure for the move was given.

squawks.headline: New York Fed reportedly intervenes in the currency market on behalf of the US Treasury
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that the New York Fed intervened in the foreign exchange market for the US Treasury. The report gives no details of the currency or amounts involved.

squawks.headline: Fed minutes show all 19 officials backed the September rate rise and most saw another 2026 hike as likely appropriate
squawks.detail: Minutes of the September FOMC meeting show almost all participants saw inflation risks tilted to the upside and job market risks as broadly balanced, and many cited risk-management grounds for the hike. Several saw the current rate as not restrictive or only mildly so; many said financial conditions still support growth despite the recent rise in long-term Treasury yields.

squawks.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent calls high bond yields a global phenomenon and says rates will fall once the Iran conflict ends
squawks.detail: The US Treasury Secretary said high bond yields are a global phenomenon and that bond yields and mortgage rates will come down once the Iran conflict ends, when he also expects the energy market to be well supplied. He also said core inflation is nearing the Fed's target.

squawks.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield reaches its highest since 2002 as global bond sell-off spreads, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the global bond sell-off on Wednesday took US 30-year borrowing costs to their highest since 2002, while UK 30-year gilt yields hit a 28-year high. The move comes three weeks before Chancellor Healey's first Budget.

squawks.headline: French PM Lecornu asks lawmakers to hold the 2027 budget deficit to 5% of GDP
squawks.detail: French Prime Minister Lecornu called on parliament to keep the 2027 deficit within 5% of GDP. The call comes during French budget talks.

squawks.headline: US $39bn 10-year note auction stops through by 1.7bp at 5.3%; bid-to-cover rises to 2.77
squawks.detail: The US Treasury's $39bn 10-year note sale drew a high yield of 5.3%, compared with 4.834% at the previous auction and a when-issued yield of 5.317% before the sale. Bid-to-cover rose to 2.77 from 2.71. Indirect bidders took 80.34%, directs 17.12% and primary dealers 2.54%.

squawks.headline: France to release 10m barrels of diesel from its strategic reserves, France Info reports
squawks.detail: French broadcaster France Info reports that France will release 10m barrels of diesel from its reserves. The report comes after IEA members backed speeding up the oil stock releases agreed in March.

squawks.headline: French Finance Ministry says there is no change to its bond issuance strategy, after WSJ report of a shift to shorter debt
squawks.detail: The French Finance Ministry said its bond issuance strategy is unchanged and follows investor demand. This comes after a WSJ report that France was considering moving issuance towards shorter-term debt amid the bond market sell-off.

squawks.headline: EU envoys sign off on about 1,650 new sanctions listings against Russia
squawks.detail: EU ambassadors have approved roughly 1,650 new listings under the Russia sanctions regime, according to EU diplomats. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: France weighs shifting issuance towards shorter-term debt amid bond market turmoil, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that France is considering issuing more short-dated debt in response to the turmoil in bond markets.

squawks.headline: NY Fed survey shows US 1-year inflation expectations up to 3.9%, above the 3.64% forecast and the previous 3.58%
squawks.detail: The New York Fed's consumer survey puts 1-year-ahead inflation expectations at 3.9%. That compares with a forecast of 3.64% and a previous reading of 3.58%.

squawks.headline: German 2-year yield falls 6bp to 3.02% while French and Italian 2-year yields rise 6bp to 3.61% and 3.48%
squawks.detail: Germany's 2-year government bond yield is down 6bp at 3.02%, against the move in other eurozone sovereign debt. France's 2-year yield is up 6bp at 3.61% and Italy's is up 6bp at 3.48%.

squawks.headline: IEA members back speeding up the oil stock releases agreed in March, with about 100m barrels still to come
squawks.detail: An IEA statement says member governments support completing the oil stock releases pledged in March as soon as possible, which would bring about 100 million barrels to market, and also back giving priority to releasing diesel stocks. Members still hold around 1.1bn barrels in reserve, including more than 200m barrels of diesel, and will review the situation at next week's governing board meeting.

squawks.headline: Polish central bank keeps its main interest rate at 3.75%, as expected
squawks.detail: Poland's central bank left its main rate unchanged at 3.75%, which matched the forecast.

squawks.headline: UK 30-year gilt yield climbs to 6.034%, its highest since 1998, up more than 12bp on the day
squawks.detail: The UK 30-year gilt yield rose to 6.034%, its highest level since 1998 and more than 12bp higher on the day, a market wire reported.

squawks.headline: Houthi rebels fire a new missile barrage at Riyadh and Aden, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports a new Houthi missile assault on the Saudi capital and on Aden. It follows a government offensive announced days earlier to retake the Bab al-Mandab waterway.

squawks.headline: Global bond sell-off resumes, with UK gilts, French and Italian bonds under pressure in volatile trading, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the global bond sell-off has resumed, with the US 30-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2002. UK, French and Italian government bonds are also reported under pressure in volatile trading; no gilt yield levels were given.

squawks.headline: Sterling falls 0.55% to $1.3205 as euro drops 0.73% to $1.1178
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reported sterling down 0.55% at $1.3205 and the euro down 0.73% at $1.1178 against the dollar.

squawks.headline: French 10-year government bond yield rises 15bp to 4.8974%
squawks.detail: A market news feed reported the French 10-year yield up 15bp on the day at 4.8974% on Wednesday morning.

squawks.headline: German 7-year Bund auction yields 3.36%, up from 2.68% last time; bid-to-cover rises to 1.4 from 1.2
squawks.detail: Germany's sale of the new 7-year Bund came in at an average yield of 3.36%, against 2.68% at the previous auction. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.4, up from 1.2.

squawks.headline: EU imposes temporary limits on imports of Chinese hybrid cars
squawks.detail: Market newswire headlines report that the EU is setting temporary caps on imports of hybrid cars from China. European carmaker shares are reported higher on the news.

squawks.headline: EUR/GBP falls 0.3% to 0.84528, its lowest level since June 2025
squawks.detail: The euro fell 0.3% against sterling to 0.84528, reaching its lowest level since June 2025, according to a market commentary account.

squawks.headline: Germany to join a further release of energy reserves under the volume the IEA set in March
squawks.detail: Germany's Economy Ministry says the country will take part in a further release of the energy reserve volume the IEA agreed in March. It says approval of the release is under way.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva calls for a prudently hawkish stance and says rate rises are still right for the Fed, ECB and BoJ
squawks.detail: The IMF Managing Director said energy and food shocks, the AI construction boom, tariffs, defence spending and high debt could add to inflation, and that global public debt is set to exceed 100% of GDP, with advanced economies carrying the heaviest burdens. She said new IMF forecasts show weaker growth in Ukraine, the Gulf states and some energy-importing economies.

squawks.headline: UK house prices flat in September at 0.0% m/m, Lloyds data show, against a 0.1% rise expected
squawks.detail: Lloyds' September house price index was unchanged on the month, below the 0.1% rise forecast in a poll.

squawks.headline: Swedish September CPI rises to 1.1% y/y, just short of the 1.2% forecast; CPIF in line at 1.5%
squawks.detail: Swedish headline CPI rose 0.9% m/m against a 1.0% forecast, and CPIF rose 1.5% y/y as expected, up from 0.7%. CPIF excluding energy held at 0.5% y/y, below the 0.7% forecast.

squawks.headline: German August industrial production rises 2% m/m, above the 0.5% forecast; annual growth of 2.3% also beats
squawks.detail: German industrial production rose 2% on the month against a 0.5% forecast, after a 1.1% fall previously. On the year, output was up 2.3%, against a 0.7% forecast and a previous reading of -1.63%.

squawks.headline: Brent crude tops $101 a barrel after more attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: City AM reports that Brent edged above $101 a barrel on Wednesday morning after attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz intensified in recent days. It adds that Middle East tensions are offsetting a rise in supply.

squawks.headline: Hedge fund industry group warns BoE that its proposed gilt repo reforms could backfire and reduce liquidity under stress
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that a hedge fund industry group has told the Bank of England its proposed reforms to the repo market, where short-term loans are secured against gilts, could cut liquidity during periods of market stress.

squawks.headline: Reserve Bank of India raises its repo rate by 25bp to 5.50%
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of India's governor said global financial market sentiment remains fragile and that there are limited signs of supply-side pressures becoming embedded. The bank raised its FY27 core inflation projection to 4.4% from 4.3%.

squawks.headline: Japan's August cash earnings rise 3.8% y/y, above the 3.7% forecast; real wages up 1.5%, an eighth straight monthly gain
squawks.detail: Japanese government data show total cash earnings up 3.8% y/y in August, against a 3.7% forecast and down from 4.7% the month before. Overtime pay rose 5.2% and inflation-adjusted real wages rose 1.5%.

squawks.headline: French Finance Minister says the government is ready to bypass parliament to pass spending cuts if budget talks stall, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: According to the Wall Street Journal, the French Finance Minister said the government is prepared to use special constitutional powers to get spending cuts through if budget negotiations stall.

squawks.headline: RBA warns a correction in AI and other shares could cut Australian household spending by 2.4%
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia says a fall in AI and other share prices could reduce household spending by 2.4%. Its documents also put the NAIRU at 4.6%, the same as the current jobless rate.

squawks.headline: UK Chancellor plans a major intervention to help poorer households with rising energy bills, Guardian reports
squawks.detail: The Guardian reports that Chancellor Healey is preparing a significant package to support lower-income households facing higher energy bills. The report gives no figures for the cost or the timing.

squawks.headline: Fed's Schmid says inflation is frustrating and must be fixed, with a way still to go; labour force seen in a good place
squawks.detail: Kansas City Fed President Schmid said the labour force remains in good shape. He also said inflation still has some way to go before it is beaten.

squawks.headline: US $58bn 3-year note auction stops through by 0.2bp at 4.932%; bid-to-cover slips to 2.62
squawks.detail: The 3-year auction's high yield was 4.932%, against a when-issued yield of 4.934% before the sale and 4.474% at the previous auction, while bid-to-cover was 2.62, down from 2.72. Indirect bidders took 57.6%, direct bidders 31.7% and primary dealers 10.7%.

squawks.headline: US EIA raises its 2026 Brent average forecast to $96.32 from $91.01 and its 2027 forecast to $83.74 from $73.74
squawks.detail: In its Short-Term Energy Outlook, the US Energy Information Administration raised its 2026 WTI average forecast to $88.21 from $84.65 and its 2027 forecast to $79.74 from $69.74. It now puts 2026 world oil demand at 102.4M b/d, down from 102.6M b/d, and 2026 world output at 101.1M b/d, up from 100.6M b/d.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly sees AI, tariffs and energy costs keeping inflation elevated and says more tightening may be needed
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said AI, tariffs and energy costs could prove longer-lasting inflation pressures and keep inflation elevated, Axios reported. She said this could mean more tightening is required.

squawks.headline: BoJ board member Sato backs raising interest rates step by step
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan board member Sato said he supports the policy of adjusting rates in stages, Kyodo reported.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kocher says energy prices are an upside risk to forecasts and names abrupt market correction and geopolitics as key risks
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Kocher said energy prices pose an upward risk to the forecasts. He also named an abrupt market correction and geopolitics as key risks.

squawks.headline: US trade deficit widens to $105.6bn, larger than the $102.05bn forecast and up from $88.6bn
squawks.detail: The US trade balance came in at -$105.6bn, against a forecast of -$102.05bn and a previous reading of -$88.6bn.

squawks.headline: ADP says US private payrolls rose by an average of 23,750 a week in the four weeks to 19 September
squawks.detail: ADP published its weekly estimate of US private-sector employment, showing an average weekly gain of 23,750 jobs over the four weeks to 19 September.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield drops 16bp and its spread over Germany narrows by 12bp
squawks.detail: A market commentary feed reports that the French 10-year government bond yield has fallen 16bp and its spread over German Bunds has narrowed by 12bp. The move comes after recent concerns about eurozone fiscal positions.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey tells banks the UK faces a difficult fiscal position and that no tax decisions have been made yet, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Healey told banks the UK's fiscal picture is difficult. She also said decisions on taxes have not yet been taken ahead of the Budget.

squawks.headline: German 2-year Schatz auction yields 3.1%, down from 3.27%, with bid-to-cover slipping to 1.1 from 1.3
squawks.detail: Germany's 2-year Schatz sale came in at an average yield of 3.1%, down from 3.27% at the previous auction. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 1.1 from 1.3.

squawks.headline: UK Treasury names Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, Morgan Stanley, NatWest and RBC Capital Markets as joint lead managers for digital gilt
squawks.detail: The UK Treasury has appointed six banks as joint lead managers for the digital gilt instrument: Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, Morgan Stanley, NatWest and RBC Capital Markets.

squawks.headline: BoE's Mann says policy must stay ahead of the curve on rate rises and the bank can tighten first and change course later if needed
squawks.detail: Bank of England MPC member Catherine Mann said policymakers need to be ahead rather than behind when raising rates. She added that the MPC can always tighten and then reverse course if required.

squawks.headline: Eurozone August retail sales rise 0.8% y/y, short of the 1% forecast; monthly gain of 0.1% also misses
squawks.detail: Eurozone retail sales grew 0.8% year on year against a 1% forecast and 0.6% previously. The month-on-month rise was 0.1%, compared with a 0.2% forecast and a previous reading of -0.6%.

squawks.headline: BoE's Mann says supply shocks are embedding inflation and the real economy is resilient
squawks.detail: Bank of England MPC member Catherine Mann said supply shocks are causing inflation to become embedded. She also said the real side of the UK economy remains resilient.

squawks.headline: UK September construction PMI rises to 46.1, above the 44.9 forecast and up from 44.3
squawks.detail: The UK construction PMI for September came in at 46.1, compared with a forecast of 44.9 and 44.3 the previous month.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham considers delaying the roadmap for raising defence spending to 3% of GDP, The Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reported on Tuesday that the Prime Minister may put back an announcement on how and when UK defence spending will rise to 3% of GDP. That step is a milestone on the way to NATO's target of 3.5% by 2035.

squawks.headline: Germany sets a 3.30% coupon on a new 7-year Bund for auction on Wednesday
squawks.detail: The Bundesbank announced a 3.30% coupon for a new 7-year Bund, which will be auctioned on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: ECB's Rehn says high long-term rates are slowing growth and that inflation has not spread to non-energy prices or wages
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Rehn said elevated long-term interest rates are weighing on growth and limiting how far energy costs pass through to other prices and wages. He added that inflation has not yet broadened to non-energy goods or salaries.

squawks.headline: Morgan Stanley puts current UK fiscal headroom at £8b and expects Healey to aim for £15b at the Budget; it is short sterling
squawks.detail: Morgan Stanley expects a small delay to fiscal consolidation at the Budget and little change to this year's cash requirement, but a slightly higher one in later years. The bank says it is shorting the pound before the Budget and sees mild downside risk for gilts.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen sets out energy steps, including a joint gas-buying task force and a one-year methane rule extension for exporters
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen announced a task force to pool energy demand, with a market operator handling joint purchases, and a one-year extension for exporters under the methane regulation. She also announced strategic talks with European refiners on costs and supply, and said state aid for energy bills should go to those who need it most.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says long-term interest rates and wider financial conditions are an important factor in monetary policy decisions
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Lane made the remarks in an interview reported by ANSA. He also said downside risks to growth have not materialised and that widespread fiscal expansion is not helping on inflation.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says the energy shock's inflation effects drove the rate decision; how far it passes through to the wider economy is uncertain
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said energy prices are high but it is uncertain how strongly they will feed through to the rest of the economy. He added that fiscal support for the economy in 2027 and 2028 will differ from 2026.

squawks.headline: French industrial production falls 0.3% m/m, missing the 0.2% rise forecast
squawks.detail: French industrial output fell 0.3% on the month, against a forecast 0.2% gain, after a 0.4% fall in the previous reading.

squawks.headline: French budget deficit widens to 159.604bn from 145.91bn in the previous reading
squawks.detail: Official French data put the budget balance at -159.604bn, compared with -145.91bn at the previous release. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: French Finance Minister Lescure says it is too early to discuss the ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument
squawks.detail: French Finance Minister Lescure said discussing use of the ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument was premature and that everything must be done to avoid reaching that point. The comments come during a continuing sell-off in French government bonds.

squawks.headline: BoJ Governor Ueda says the underlying price trend is nearing 2% and Japan's economy is recovering moderately
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said Japan's economy is recovering moderately despite some weaknesses and that business sentiment is favourable. He also said the underlying price trend is approaching 2%.

squawks.headline: German August factory orders fall 10.6% m/m, far worse than the 1% drop forecast
squawks.detail: German industrial orders fell 10.6% month on month in August, against a forecast fall of 1% and a 2.5% rise the month before. Working-day adjusted orders rose 2.7% year on year, against a forecast of 13.1% and 13.1% previously.

squawks.headline: Many BoJ officials are cautious about an October rate rise, though the bank may say underlying inflation has about reached 2%, sources say
squawks.detail: People familiar with the Bank of Japan's thinking say many policymakers are wary of raising rates at the October meeting. The same sources say the bank may indicate at that meeting that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2% target.

squawks.headline: Japan's 10-year JGB auction tail narrows to 0.02 from 0.12 at the previous sale; 10-year yield cuts its rise to 1.5bp at 3.1%
squawks.detail: After the auction, 10-year JGB futures cut their losses to 0.18 yen at 124.32. The 20-year yield cut its gain to 1bp at 3.98%.

squawks.headline: Japan raises its 10-year JGB coupon to 3.1%, the highest in about 30 years, for a ¥2.6tn offering
squawks.detail: Japan's Ministry of Finance is offering ¥2.6 trillion of 10-year government bonds with a 3.100% coupon, which Kyodo reports is the highest in about 30 years. The 30-year JGB yield was reported at a record 4.24%, up 1bp, and the 5-year yield rose 3bp to 2.39%.

squawks.headline: Yemeni government forces say they have retaken Mocha from the Houthis and pushed them out of areas around Bab el-Mandeb
squawks.detail: Yemen's internationally recognised forces say they took back the Red Sea port city after heavy fighting. Saudi-backed forces have launched a counteroffensive to regain control of the strait.

squawks.headline: Trump signs order letting anyone buy tax-free red-dyed diesel by waiving the off-road requirement
squawks.detail: The US President signed the executive order on the evening of 5 October, US time. He said its aim is to contain near-record diesel prices.

squawks.headline: New York Fed reviews big banks' lending to private credit firms, including Barclays, Semafor reports
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that New York Fed officials have visited JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley. They asked about the banks' exposure to private credit firms, their risk management and the quality of collateral.

squawks.headline: US Treasury warns foreign banks they could face sanctions for doing business with Iran
squawks.detail: The US Treasury has sent an alert to foreign financial institutions that deal with Iran, saying they could be sanctioned. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Yemen's Houthis claim control of Bab al-Mandab, Dhubab and al-Mukha, Iranian agency ISNA reports
squawks.detail: Iran's ISNA news agency carried the Houthi claim that Bab al-Mandab, Dhubab and al-Mukha are under the group's control. The inputs report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Euro falls to its lowest level against the dollar since May 2025 as Spain's snap election adds to eurozone fiscal worries
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that the euro fell to its weakest level against the dollar since May 2025. It says Spain's snap elections have added to growing fiscal and political concerns across the eurozone.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises to 5.34%, a new high since 2002
squawks.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.34%, its highest level since 2002, according to a market news feed on Monday afternoon.

squawks.headline: Bank of France governor Moulin warns rising interest costs could overwhelm French state finances, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports that Bank of France governor Emmanuel Moulin warned the French state risks being choked by interest rates. The comments follow the recent French government bond sell-off.

squawks.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield climbs to 5.69%, its highest level since 2002
squawks.detail: Market reports show the US 30-year Treasury yield rising to 5.69%, a new high since 2002.

squawks.headline: Trump to set out plan easing use of tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, officials say
squawks.detail: US officials say President Trump will unveil a plan on Monday to ease restrictions on the use of red-dyed, tax-exempt diesel. No further details were given.

squawks.headline: US September ISM services PMI falls to 54.9, just under the 55.0 forecast and down from 55.4
squawks.detail: The ISM non-manufacturing index for September came in at 54.9, against a consensus estimate of 55.0 and a previous reading of 55.4.

squawks.headline: US final September services PMI is revised up to 58.8 from the 58.7 flash; composite PMI unchanged at 58.4
squawks.detail: The S&P Global survey shows services rising from 56.5 in August and the composite from 56.0. The survey reports new order growth at a four-and-a-half-year high, the fastest job creation since June 2022 and input cost inflation picking up again.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says new ONS estimates point to much stronger UK productivity growth since the financial crisis
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says revised estimates from the ONS imply UK productivity has grown considerably faster since the financial crisis than previously thought. The post gave no figures.

squawks.headline: Yemen's armed forces say they have launched a strategic offensive in Sanaa
squawks.detail: Yemen's armed forces announced the start of what they called a strategic offensive in Sanaa. The announcement follows strikes by the Saudi-led coalition and Houthi attacks on Saudi Aramco sites. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition says 100 fighter jets struck 324 targets in Yemen and it is giving air cover to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said in statements that 100 fighter jets took part in an operation in Yemen that hit 324 targets it described as high-value. It also said it is providing air protection for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

squawks.headline: Eurozone August producer prices rise 8.2% y/y, above the 7.9% forecast; monthly rise of 1.9% is in line
squawks.detail: Eurozone producer price inflation climbed to 8.2% year on year from 5.8% previously, ahead of the 7.9% forecast. On the month, prices rose 1.9%, matching expectations, after a 1.6% rise previously.

squawks.headline: Saudi East-West oil pipeline is reported to be running normally again after an earlier halt
squawks.detail: People familiar with the matter say oil is flowing as normal through Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. The blotter earlier reported that the pipeline had been halted after a new attack. No market reaction has been reported yet.

squawks.headline: Saudi East-West oil pipeline halted after a new attack; Brent recovers earlier losses
squawks.detail: Market reports say a fresh attack has stopped Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Brent crude was reported to have recovered its earlier losses on the news.

squawks.headline: UK final September services PMI revised up to 52.1 from 51.7 flash; composite PMI final at 52
squawks.detail: The final UK services PMI for September came in at 52.1 and the composite at 52, both above the 51.7 forecast and the 51.7 previous reading.

squawks.headline: Aramco CEO says upstream facilities are intact and maximum output capacity of 12M b/d can be reached within days
squawks.detail: Saudi Aramco's chief executive commented on the state of the company's upstream facilities after the Houthi attacks on Aramco sites. He said its maximum oil output capacity of 12M barrels a day is available within days.

squawks.headline: Eurozone final September services PMI is 53 and composite 53.1, both in line with forecasts; German composite final at 53.8
squawks.detail: The eurozone final services PMI came in at 53 and the composite at 53.1, matching forecasts and the previous readings. Germany's final services PMI was 52.9 and its composite 53.8, also matching forecasts and the previous readings.

squawks.headline: French September services PMI comes in at 51.2, slightly below the 51.4 forecast; composite PMI at 51.1
squawks.detail: France's services PMI was 51.2, against a forecast and previous reading of 51.4. The composite PMI was 51.1, against a forecast and previous reading of 51.2.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says upside risks dominate the inflation outlook and uncertainty calls for flexibility rather than inaction
squawks.detail: Bundesbank President and ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said there are no clear signs yet of inflation feeding into price and wage setting. He also said Germany has entered a gradual recovery.

squawks.headline: Italy's September services PMI falls to 51.7, well below the 54.5 forecast; composite PMI drops to 51
squawks.detail: Italy's services PMI came in at 51.7, against a forecast of 54.5 and down from 55.2. The composite PMI was 51, against a forecast of 53.2 and down from 53.6.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi rules out deficit-financing bonds to fund the sales tax and pledges to manage annual debt issuance effectively
squawks.detail: Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi said the government will not use deficit-financing bonds to fund the sales tax, will manage yearly debt issuance effectively and will draw up a five-year investment plan by the end of the year. She also said the government will respond quickly if the economy or markets move unexpectedly.

squawks.headline: Middle East crude exports exceed pre-war levels despite rising attacks on tankers, shipping data show
squawks.detail: Shipping data published on Monday show Middle East crude exports were above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the final week of September. Attacks on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz have increased over the same period.

squawks.headline: Japan's 30-year JGB yield rises 2.5bp to a record high of 4.23%
squawks.detail: The 30-year Japanese government bond yield rose 2.5bp to 4.23% in early Asian trade on Monday, a record high.

squawks.headline: Global LNG spot prices hit highest since late 2022 as Qatar extends force majeure on LNG contracts
squawks.detail: Spot LNG prices have reached their highest since late 2022 as Qatar's supply freeze continues and it extends force majeure on LNG contracts. Maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz is reported down 80% from February.

squawks.headline: Apache offshore workers vote to strike, which could disrupt the North Sea Forties pipeline, Unite says
squawks.detail: The Unite union said more than 160 offshore workers at Apache back strike action this month that could disrupt the Forties pipeline, a major route for UK oil and gas supplies.

squawks.headline: Brent climbs to $103.06 a barrel after Yemen's Houthis attack Saudi Aramco sites
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Brent crude futures rose to $103.06 a barrel in early Asian trading after Houthi attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities.

squawks.headline: EY fiscal forecast shows Iran war could fully erase Healey's headroom against borrowing rule
squawks.detail: City AM reports that EY's central fiscal forecast shows the Chancellor's buffer against the borrowing target has shrunk and could be wiped out by the effects of the Iran war. Economists also said the OBR could take a gloomier view of the UK economy.

squawks.headline: UK expected to impose tariffs on Chinese electric cars, The Times reports
squawks.detail: Reuters, citing The Times on Sunday, says Britain is expected to put tariffs on electric vehicles imported from China.

squawks.headline: Bundesbank's Nagel says German growth this year could reach about 1%, around twice recent projections
squawks.detail: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said on Friday that strong export demand and government investment could lift German growth to around 1% this year, roughly double the latest projections, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Healey expected to use the Budget for targeted support rather than large tax rises, putting off hard choices, FT reports
squawks.detail: According to the Financial Times, Chancellor Healey is expected to centre her Budget statement on targeted help for households and businesses. The paper says she is not expected to raise taxes on the scale of recent Budgets.

squawks.headline: Hedge funds hold a net short position in sterling for the first time since 2024, CFTC data show
squawks.detail: Weekly CFTC positioning data released on Friday show hedge funds have moved to a net short position in the pound for the first time since 2024.

squawks.headline: Trump rules out a US ban on diesel exports
squawks.detail: US President Trump said on Friday that the administration will not impose a ban on diesel exports.

squawks.headline: US Justice Department will not reopen its criminal investigation into Fed Chair Powell, Attorney General says
squawks.detail: Attorney General Blanche said the Department of Justice is satisfied with the Fed inspector general's report and will not resume the criminal probe into Powell.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee keeps both a rate rise and a pause open, saying the inflation side of the Fed's mandate matters more
squawks.detail: Speaking to Fox Business, Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the labour market is steady and he wants to see whether there is evidence that inflation is heading back to 2%. He added that he would not react strongly to a single month of data.

squawks.headline: Italy plans to ask the EU for 2027 deficit leeway of 0.6% of GDP and raises its 2026 growth forecast to 0.8%
squawks.detail: Italy's government plans to ask the EU for deficit flexibility worth 0.6% of GDP in 2027, and expects the 2026 deficit to come in below 3% of GDP. It also raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.8%, up from the 0.6% it forecast in April.

squawks.headline: IEA head Birol says oil prices fell at least $5 after the agency announced a release of oil and diesel reserves
squawks.detail: IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said the stocks will go to market over the coming days and weeks, with distribution to be finalised after consultation with member states. He said reserves are sufficient and more can be released if needed.

squawks.headline: French-German 10-year bond yield spread narrows to 140bp from 159bp
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that the gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields has fallen to 140bp from 159bp.

squawks.headline: Macron says the G7 has decided to release up to 100mn barrels of diesel and crude stocks over four months
squawks.detail: French President Macron said G7 countries have agreed to release strategic diesel and crude stocks of up to 100mn barrels. He said the release will take place over four months.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says the administration does not aim to inflate its way out of debt and puts higher yields down to a strong…
squawks.detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said US interest payments are too high, the President is committed to cutting the deficit and the jobs report was in line with expectations. He said yields are higher because the economy is strong.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says the US Navy has reopened the Strait of Hormuz and crude is flowing through
squawks.detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said the US Navy has reopened the Strait of Hormuz and crude oil is passing through again. He added that more energy announcements will follow next week. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Fed-dated swaps stop fully pricing one more US rate rise this year
squawks.detail: Fed-dated swaps no longer price a full Federal Reserve rate rise by the end of the year, according to a market post. This comes after earlier moves that priced out an October rise.

squawks.headline: US September unemployment rate rises to 4.2% against 4.1% forecast; annual wage growth slows to 3.0%
squawks.detail: The US September jobs report shows unemployment at 4.2%, average hourly earnings up 3.0% y/y and a two-month net payroll revision of minus 60,000. US short-term rate futures jumped after the release as traders cut bets on an October Fed rate rise.

squawks.headline: US September nonfarm payrolls rise 29,000, well short of the 84,000 consensus
squawks.detail: The US Labor Department reports September nonfarm payrolls up 29,000, against a consensus forecast of 84,000. Average weekly hours are 34.4, compared with a 34.3 forecast and unchanged from the previous month.

squawks.headline: French 2-year government bond yield rises 13.8bp to 3.8337% as the French bond sell-off extends
squawks.detail: France's 2-year government bond yield was last up 13.8bp on the day at 3.8337%. The move follows earlier rises in French 10-year yields and a widening in French CDS.

squawks.headline: French 10-year government bond yield reaches 4.989%, its highest level since 2002
squawks.detail: LSEG data show the French 10-year yield at 4.989%, the highest since 2002, as the French bond sell-off continues.

squawks.headline: Diesel prices drop sharply as EU weighs releasing 50mn barrels of reserves under US pressure, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports the EU is considering releasing 50mn barrels of diesel reserves after the US president threatened to ban US diesel exports if Europe does not release stocks. Diesel prices were reported to have fallen sharply; no release has been agreed.

squawks.headline: NIESR says about two-thirds of the third-quarter rise in 10-year gilt yields came from higher rate expectations
squawks.detail: NIESR's latest Term Premium Tracker puts the UK 10-year gilt yield at 5.43% at the end of the quarter, its highest since 2007. It estimates that about two-thirds of the increase came from higher expected interest rates, with the rest from term premium.

squawks.headline: UK average diesel price passes £2 a litre for the first time, RAC says
squawks.detail: The RAC reports the average UK diesel pump price has gone above £2 per litre, a level not reached before.

squawks.headline: France's bond risk premium widens to 150bp, a level last seen in 2012
squawks.detail: A market commentator reports that France's sovereign bond risk premium has reached 150bp for the first time since 2012. French bonds are selling off this week after the 2027 budget was presented.

squawks.headline: French 5-year sovereign CDS widen further to 81bp
squawks.detail: S&P Global Market Intelligence data show French 5-year credit default swaps at 81bp, up from the 71.6bp reported earlier, which was already the highest since July 2013.

squawks.headline: Eurozone September flash CPI rises to 3.8% y/y, above 3.7% forecast and up from 3.2%; core holds in line at 2.5%
squawks.detail: The eurozone flash estimate puts September headline inflation at 3.8% year on year, against a 3.7% forecast and 3.2% previously, and at 0.6% month on month, against a 0.5% forecast. Core inflation rose to 2.5% from 2.4%, matching the forecast.

squawks.headline: FAO says world food prices rose in September to their highest level in nearly four years
squawks.detail: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization says its world food price measure climbed in September to a near four-year high. It points to logistics disruptions and weather concerns in crop markets as the causes.

squawks.headline: BoE Decision Maker Panel: firms see year-ahead CPI at 3.3% in September, with expected wage growth steady at 3.4%
squawks.detail: The Bank of England's Decision Maker Panel survey puts firms' year-ahead CPI inflation expectations at 3.3% for September. Firms' expected wage growth for the year ahead held at 3.4% in the three months to September.

squawks.headline: UK 2-year gilt yield drops 9bp to 4.726%, its lowest level since 22 September
squawks.detail: The 2-year gilt yield fell 9bp to 4.726% in early trading on 2 October, its lowest since 22 September, according to a market wire post.

squawks.headline: ECB's Rehn says higher energy prices are bringing inflation closer to the ECB's adverse scenario
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn said rising energy prices were moving the inflation outlook nearer to the central bank's adverse scenario. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: DMO announces ad hoc tender of up to £1.5bn of a 2028 gilt on 7 October
squawks.detail: The UK Debt Management Office says it will hold an ad hoc tender of up to £1.5bn of a 2028 gilt on 7 October.

squawks.headline: Japan's economy minister says extraordinary monetary stimulus is no longer needed as Japan is out of deflation
squawks.detail: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi said overly loose monetary policy is no longer required and that the Takaichi government aims for both growth and fiscal discipline. He said monetary policy is for the BoJ and he hopes it keeps in close contact with the government.

squawks.headline: Dollar holds at 17-month high, heading for a third weekly gain, as the global bond sell-off weighs on the euro
squawks.detail: Reuters reports the dollar at a 17-month high, with borrowing costs around the world at multi-decade peaks on inflation concerns linked to higher oil prices. The euro has weakened below $1.1250 ahead of US payrolls data.

squawks.headline: Tokyo September CPI rises to 2.7% y/y, above forecasts, as core inflation reaches its fastest rate since November 2025
squawks.detail: Japanese government data show headline Tokyo CPI at 2.7%, against a 2.5% forecast and 1.9% previously. Core CPI also rose to 2.7% from 1.8%, and the measure excluding fresh food and energy was 3.0%; the national August jobless rate came in at 2.5%, against a forecast of 2.4%.
